transcript.text: Gas oven took ages to light tonight then went WHOOMPH and now the kitchen smells really strongly of gas even though I've turned it off. Is it safe to try again?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
If you can smell gas, treat it as an emergency: don't turn any switches on or off and no naked flames. Turn the gas off at the meter if you safely can, open doors and windows, and leave if the smell is strong. Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999.
ok I'm panicking a bit. The smell is still really strong. Meter box is outside by the front door, should I turn it off there? Also it's a rented house and I can't contact the landlord tonight

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Yes—if the meter box is outside and you can reach it without going back through the kitchen, turn the gas off at the meter using the emergency control valve. Turn the handle a quarter-turn so it is across the pipe, not in line with it. Do not use any electrical switches, plugs, doorbells or phones inside the property. Then move away from the house and call the Gas Emergency Service on 0800 111 999. Tell them the gas oven was slow to light, ignited with a whoomph, and the smell is still strong. Do not try the oven again or turn the gas back on. The eventual cause could be a faulty ignition or gas-control component, but it must be made safe and diagnosed by the emergency engineer/Gas Safe engineer first.

reading.symptom: Took a long time to light, then ignited with a whoomph; strong gas smell remains after being turned off

claimsRejected.claim: A very strong smell that remains after the cooker is off needs their urgent attendance; it is not something to wait for the landlord to deal with tonight.

candidates: Gas leak or unburnt gas following delayed ignition (high)
Gas oven ignition or gas-control fault (medium)
plan: They asked: "Should I turn it off at the meter box outside by the front door?" - answer that first.

Safety: they reported a gas smell earlier and were given the emergency advice. Do not repeat it. Do not suggest any check or use of the appliance; answer what they ask now, and make sure they know to keep following that advice until a Gas Safe engineer has made it safe.

The fault they reported is: "Took a long time to light, then ignited with a whoomph; strong gas smell remains after being turned off". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
